cls: Centrally and peripherally acting non-opioid antitussive
pharm: Non-opioid cough suppressant; the levorotatory isomer of cloperastine acting on the medullary cough centre with peripheral antitussive (antihistaminic/antispasmodic) and bronchial soothing activity
quick: 20 mg (e.g. 10 mL syrup of 20 mg/10 mL) three times daily
May be taken with or without food
Cough response; drowsiness; review if cough persists >1 week
summary: Levocloperastine is a non-opioid antitussive (the active levorotatory isomer of cloperastine) used for the symptomatic relief of non-productive (dry) cough. It acts centrally on the medullary cough centre and peripherally through antihistaminic/antispasmodic effects on the bronchial mucosa, without the dependence and constipation risks of opioid antitussives and with relatively little sedation. It is commonly used in India and parts of Europe and is NOT FDA-approved; information here is based on SmPC/manufacturer prescribing data. It should not be used for productive cough where expectoration is needed, and persistent cough warrants evaluation.
indications: Symptomatic relief of non-productive (dry, irritating) cough of various origins

dosage.d: 20 mg three times daily (commonly 10 mL of a 20 mg/10 mL syrup TID)

dosage.c: Dry cough - children (per local pediatric syrup labeling)
dosage.d: Pediatric syrup dose by age/weight as per product label (e.g. 5 mL two to three times daily in older children)
dosage.n: Follow the specific pediatric product label; avoid in young infants

dosage.d: Use the lowest effective dose with caution

admin: Take by mouth with or without food; measure syrup with the supplied measuring device
Use for short-term symptomatic relief of dry cough only - not for productive/chesty cough
Do not combine with expectorants/mucolytics for the same episode (suppressing a productive cough can cause secretion retention)
Re-evaluate if cough persists beyond about one week or is associated with high fever, rash or persistent headache
moa: Levocloperastine suppresses cough through a central action on the medullary cough centre and a peripheral action on the bronchial mucosa (antihistaminic and antispasmodic/smooth-muscle relaxant effects that reduce bronchial irritation). Unlike opioid antitussives it lacks significant analgesic, respiratory-depressant or dependence-producing activity.

relative: Productive (chesty) cough where retaining secretions would be harmful
monitor: Need for further investigation if cough persists

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; avoid use unless considered essential by a physician. (Not an FDA-approved product; based on SmPC guidance.)
lact: It is not known whether levocloperastine is excreted in human milk; avoid use during breastfeeding because safety has not been established.
renal: There is limited data in renal impairment; use with caution.
hepatic: There is limited data in hepatic impairment; use with caution as the drug is hepatically metabolized.

moderate: CNS depressants (sedatives, hypnotics, opioids, antihistamines, alcohol) - additive sedation/drowsiness
minor: Expectorants/mucolytics - opposing actions; avoid using together for a productive cough
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food

emergency: Signs of a severe allergic reaction (swelling of face/throat, difficulty breathing, widespread rash)

monitoring: Persistence of cough beyond about one week - reassess for an underlying cause
counsel: Use for dry, irritating cough only and for short periods; this is not for a chesty/productive cough
It may cause mild drowsiness - be cautious driving or operating machinery and avoid alcohol
Measure liquid doses with the provided measuring device, not a kitchen spoon
See a doctor if the cough lasts more than about a week, or comes with high fever, rash or persistent headache
Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding unless your doctor advises
Keep out of reach of children
pk: Antitussive effect within about 20-30 minutes of dosing
Plasma peak roughly 1-2 hours after an oral dose
Short (a few hours), consistent with three-times-daily dosing
Cough suppression of several hours; dose three times daily
Store at room temperature, protected from light; keep the bottle tightly closed and out of reach of children
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - widely used in India and parts of Europe; information here is from SmPC/manufacturer data rather than openFDA
Non-opioid antitussive (levo-isomer of cloperastine) - relieves dry cough without opioid dependence/constipation and with relatively little sedation
Do not use for productive cough or combine with expectorants - suppressing a chesty cough can cause secretion retention
Investigate cough that persists beyond ~1 week or with red-flag features rather than continuing symptomatic suppression
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose may cause marked drowsiness, dizziness and gastrointestinal upset. Management is supportive (airway, observation); there is no specific antidote. Contact a poison control center, especially in children.
